body: Although we just got there in the middle of the day we could see many animals including an armadillo.Especially the tour with a guide was great for the kids although they didn't understand English he did great
title: Super for kids

body: We were so lucky to be with Poorna on the night tour. We saw two lorris, including one capturing and eating a butterfly. We also saw a brown wood owl and a spotted mouse deer. What an amazing experience!
title: Amazing night tour

body: Excellent place to visit, historical site, neat and clean fairly small and local people are providing a great service to visitors / tourists.Several trails available. Night time is best we were told. Day time some of those trails are closed. We did the day time trail and finished within 30mins, steady pace.NOTE: entrance fees are 1000 Sri Lankan Rupees (for all ages). Very decent value for a small trek. Fees are not advertised anywhere but we found that out on the site / entrance.
title: Popham's Arboretum, Entrance Fees and Trail Map + Details

body: Popham Arboretum is a peaceful forest retreat near Sigiriya, best known for its elusive and adorable slender lorises. Walking the trails with expert guides, you’ll also enjoy native trees and a variety of birds. A quiet, unique spot for nature lovers and photographers — truly a hidden gem!
title: Slow Loris, A Must-See for Wildlife Lovers

body: What is really interesting is the night safari that is held here, where knowledgeable guides show you the rare Loris. During the day you can also see the terrain with a guide: but definitely think about mosquito repellent, otherwise you will be eaten. I didn't find it very exciting during the day. But the Lorissafari is great, brings a flashlight and trip-proof shoes, it's really pitch black dark
title: Be sure to make the Nightsafari the Loris

body: Extraordinary experience where we just spontaneously decided in Colombo at 2pm.and left at 3pmOur interaction with Chanaka at Popham was excellent and he gave this option of villa which was Sri Lankan rate unbelievable rate. I told him that I read the reviews and this person Poorna was mentioned as an excellent guide and we would like him for the night safari.We arrive at Popham at 7:20pm post lots of stops and even having a pizza at pizza hut Dambulla Chanaka greeted us introduced to Poorna and Nimal the two trackers.Now the crazy part is we being wild life awareness were so not geared for this night safari we were slippons (rubber slipper) Nevertheless Poorna was made aware of our attire and he took extreme cautious of the route and spotting. We spotted1. Cute baby Loris2. 5 Loris adults in various places3. Scorpions many4. Shikaka Cave experience if anyone has seen ace Ventura5. Amazing stay at the villa with the sounds of the Loris mainly and also other owls etc.6. Authentic Breakfast (of course I know what we want so just gave Poorna a list and he helped get the best breakfast for us)The expedition was my 15 yr old idea. I just make things happen.Also if you love lightning views then while travelling to Dambulla we experience the most amazing lightning views ever far on the mountains.We also visited CIc Dambulla I think I need to be a tour guide 😍😜😂 because my experience are beyond the standard stuff my 15yr old says as once with me it is an adventure of a life time. All and all Chanaka also gave use Popham bees honey with comb and this was mind blowing.
title: Loris Night adventure and villa stay at Popham Dambulla

body: We were so disappointed when heavy rain arrived on the evening we planned to go on the Loris walk. Yohan, our guide from Gracious Lanka called the Arboretum team and rearranged the walk for 4am the next morning. A team of at least four staff were out looking for the Loris. We were lucky to see three Loris on our walk, one in particular gave us excellent views. The staff were so helpful and enthusiastic, particularly as this was the first time they had conducted an early morning walk. We also saw mouse deer and a rufous horseshoe bat roost. We highly recommend the Loris walk and if we'd had more time we would have visited the Arboretum during the day to see the wide variety of other wildlife that live there.
title: Early morning Grey Slender Loris walk

body: What a surprise ! An absolutely wonderful experience. We went on the night tour to see the Loris, a rare and incredibly cute creature. The guides walks with you through the dark forest and has a magical gift to spot this tiny creatures in the trees. Probably a once in a lifetime experience.Every nature lover will love this tour ! Apart from this, I think the Arboretum team is doing a marvellous job to keep this oasis alive.
title: Night walk to see the Loris

body: We had the most amazing experience tonight. We went with the aspiration of seeing a loris. We were amazed to see not one, but five, including some babies. The skill and knowledge of the guides is incredible. They were also so courteous. It was a real highlight and one I would recommend to any wildlife enthusiast.Such incredible value.
title: Amazing experience thanks to skilled and charming guides.

body: Absolutely brilliant So pleased we found this trip !Our guide was so knowledgeable and he was so excited when he spotted a loris with baby for us to see !!Such a valuable place for flora and faunaAnd to think that Mr popham developed the area then donated it to the Sri Lankan government - what a special man !!
title: Night tour - wear covered shoes - take mosquito repellent and a red lamp torch if possible !!

body: We had a great night safari with our guide Poorna. He had an amazing ability to find a loris immediately and several mouse deer.
title: Night safari

body: A beautiful night out in 1 natural site! Thanks to the professionalism of the guide and his indispensable help, we saw: 4 lorises (very tall in trees), dears, mouse dears, civet......
title: To do for those who love wildlife!

body: Thoroughly enjoyed the evening walk through the jungle. Saw 2 x loris, several creepy crawlies and the shining eyes of a mouse deer. Enthusiastic guides lead you through the bush and somehow manage to spot a loris or two if you're lucky, as we were. Wear long trousers and decent walking shoes/boots as most of the time you cannot see what you're walking on/in though the guide will flash a torch for more challenging bits. Good prewalk film explains the arboretum. Not at all touristy, guide just took my wife and I alone and there were 3 in the 2nd group.
title: Genuine night hike through natural forest with a once in a lifetime opportunity to see a loris or two

body: If you love nature this is far and beyond the best experience in Sri Lanka. An intimate exploration of a rich habitat with an expert guide. We did not feel like tourists, we were explorers. Poorna was so knowledgeable and passionate about the flora and fauna, we only wished we could have stayed longer and hope to return next year. Absolutely brilliant.
title: Absolutely Brilliant!

body: Spent a lovely couple of hours here. The whole concept of re-wilding was unheard of back in the 60s when Sam set this up. In fact the concept became known as the Popham method. Now it is a mature wilderness with easy to follow paths and a great variety of wildlife. We visited during the day but I would recommend a night visit too to see the elusive super cute Loris if you can. Well worth supporting this project.
title: Fantastic restored wilderness full of nature

body: Visited during the day, and we liked it so much we changed our plans to make another visit during the night happen 😀 Very calming experience, we cannot recommend it enough, if you are looking for ethical safari without crowds of people! The staff is superb: broad knowledge, passionate about their work, honest and kind people! (Thank you Poorna, you were GREAT!!)Day tour:- at start theres short introduction video (nice, high quality equipment 👌) and guide introduction- opportunity to say hi to 2 different species of tiny bats- you can choose one of 4 tours thru the forest, which you explore on your own- we saw giant squirrels, birds, jungle chickens. It was so nice to explore and enjoy nature in its real form ❤️ I would say - dont expect zoo-like experience, its a matter of luck what you will see- after coming back, we shared our findings with guide and got refreshments - paid 1k lkr per person (entry tickets)Night tour:- its recommended to get there a bit earlier (contact arboretum for details), to make whole process smooth. We got there 6-7 pm- short introduction, the small group gathered and we dived into the forest with 2 guides equipped with redlights and flashlights - guides know the arboretum well and know where to look to find deers, mongoose and local star: slow loris- animals and guests are treated with much respect and I really appreciate that 🙏- the price of the ticket is 2.5k lkr per personWe will definitely come back!
title: Thats how animal watching should look like!

body: The night tour was one of the highlights of our holiday in Sri Lanka! Popham's Arboretum is little-known gem - staff at our hotel were not aware of it not were other travellers we spoke to. Avoid the (much) more expensive tours to see the Slender Loris - this place is inexpensive, tour guides are scientists and you can see many types of animals. We saw slender loris, mouse deer, civet and fireflies. A truly wonderful experience.
title: HIghlight of our holiday

body: Such an amazing night tour! We saw a civet, mouse deer and the highlight, a loris. The park is spectacular at night and our guide was friendly and knowledgeable. A bargain at 2500 rupees pp. Definitely a highlight of our trip!
title: Night tour

body: We popped in during the day to see the house that Geoffery Bawa designed (pretty cool) and to see a 400+ year old ebony tree. Then learned about the night safari led by the facility coordinator and costing much less than the ones offered by the hotels. We came back that night and walked the arboretum in a small group, silently discovering lots of animals including a tiny mouse deer and a loris. Overall we had a really pleasant experience here. Highly recommended for folks who want to learn about the native flora and fauna.
title: "loris at night" walking tour was really fun

body: Didn’t have an opportunity to visit at night. So that tour might be much interesting. Foods are delivered by a nearby house which is really delicious.
title: Great service

body: This is an excellent government-run small reserve with local guides, one of whom had worked on the project since inception in the 80s. Our homestay host found it for us as a MUCH cheaper and more ethical alternative to the hotel-run loris night trails, and it was well worth the time. We arrived later than the 6:30om start, so they charged us only 2500 rupees each compared to $40 at the hotel. Normally we were told it costs 4000 rupees each and lasts for a few hours. We saw many slow lorises, bats and mouse deer and normally they are able to see pangolins too. The money is reinvested in the conservation project and this felt so much more worthwhile than a weirdly inflated hotel tour. And if you see no wildlife, which is basically impossible, the walk round the reserve by torchlight is extremely beautiful and calming, with some lovely star-gazing and wildlife sounds. Highly recommend.
title: Unexpected cheap gem of a find- many lorises!

body: A friend recommended this beautiful hidden jungle-garden. We walked there for more than an hour and saw so many different trees and bird. For architects it‘s very nice to see the main building by the famous Geoffrey Bawa.
title: Jungle and Architecture

body: Well the daytime walk for us was worth the Rs 1000 (USD5), but as we're not naturalists and more used to botanical gardens it was on the edge. By being deliberately as natural and basic as possible, with just pathways cut (with signage) and only some main trees near the entrance having nameplates, it's a heaven for naturalists. Not too much interesting for normal tourists. As the paths are a bit rough (esp. the crossings of the small stream) and not easy to walk even by daytime, and we don't own cameras with good night shots, we skipped the option of an evening tour for Loris and Pangolin.
title: Great for naturalists

body: We visited the reserve for an evening walk to find loris. The guide firstly told us how the park was developed, very informative, then we set off to find the loris with 2 guides. On route we managed to see a snake, deer and eventually loris, how the guide spotted the little creature is incredible, years of experience I guess. This was a different adventure but well worth it. Definitely recommend this place
title: Find the loris

body: We loved our visit to Popham's arboretum! We arrived in the late afternoon and explored the arboretum during daytime (we saw some giant squirrel, monitor lizard and birds) and did an evening safari after. The park is really beautiful, informative and easy to walk. Mr Poorna and Mr Chanaka were really passionate and helped us spot four loris and a mouse deer. We're happy we went here during our stay in Dambulla/Sigiriya.
title: Great to see loris and other animals

body: This is a must-visit place around Dambulla for nature lovers. Many different animals inside a relatively small space. However, the yellow route we took, took around 1hour to walk. There are many places around to snap a nice photo. The caretaker is very informative. You can give a donation of your choice to help maintain the place
title: Spend an hour with nature

body: After being asked for a 1000 LKR donation per person we decided to skip the arboretum. They called it a donation, but when it is mandatory it should be called an entrance ticket, there is no voluntary element. The park looked nice, but paying $20 for a 2-hour walk in the forest is too much. I'm all in for supporting nice causes with a donation, but this is not the way to ask for money. Donation is voluntary, the amount decided by the person giving the money. Demanding a fixed price for something cannot be called a donation.
title: Find another park for a walk and save money

body: "Madam, Madam come quick" the guide would urgently whisper to my wife! He would be pointing out a fishing cat or deer or the Slender Loris! We got a good picture (they are small and fairly high in the trees, so had to us night-shot-handheld setting on the camera with a zoom). All well worth the walk in the dark and the guide made it fun.
title: Cool forest with Slender Loris!

body: Called the mobile number to arrange the visit. We arrived and went into a little office area where the gentleman explained how the place started up etc. We were given a torch and off we went. If there's a few of you I'd advise taking your own torches or phones.We went for a walk in the woods with 2 guides. They are very good at spotting the loris. Managed to find one but it was too quick for us to see. We then wandered around for a good hour and a bit, we only saw a deer. But the owner didnt accept any money as we didn't see anything which was kind. He just asked for us to tip his assistant.A nice little adventure but I think you have to be lucky to see the loris
title: Walk in the dark

body: We left with my brother at night to see the slow loris in late December. We have not been disappointed. After a long walk to search we saw 4 of which 2 very visible. Possibility of making good images with flashlights. Passionate and very friendly guides and directors. Thanks again. It was my dream to see this animal.
title: Good place to see the loris

body: This is an amazing conservation project, interesting for anyone interested in nature and the environment. Our time was limited, but I would have liked to have had a couple of hours there. It was really enjoyable experience. In addition to the wonderful plants and trees, the house there is if interest. It was designed by the well known architect, Geoffery Bawa.We were taken around (whistle stop tour as we were short of time) by the manager Jayanthe Amerasinghe and saw a lot in a short time. Mr Amerasinghe is an extremely knowledgable horticulturalist, engaging and enthusiastic. We learnt a lot about uses of the local trees and plants for medicines or herbs. The whole place is a great example of supported regeneration of the native vegetation. (university students spend time there conducting research and supporting the work). Much recommend a visit here, preferably with a couple of hours to spare. You can also arrange to go on a night walk, and possibly see Slow Loris amongst other animals. (sounds great!). There is a suggested small donation (1000 SL rupees, about US$7) to help with the conservation work. Well worth it.
title: such and interesting, tranquil and beautiful place

body: We phoned the manager to arrange the night walk. It was very quick and easy to setup the tour. The two guides were absolutely brilliant! We saw four Loris and a mouse deer in 1.5 hours. A truly magical experience. Thank you!
title: Fantastic experience to see the Loris and mouse deer

body: Went on the night time walk and had an amazing time. More than happy to recommend our guide, Poorna Tharaka, who was friendly, knowledgeable, and charismatic, with a sixth sense for spotting wildlife in the dark! Saw six (six!) Slow Loris, as well as a family of spotted deer, a false vampire bat, and a beautiful firefly display. Highly recommended, you feel much closer to nature than you do on a Jeep Safari.
title: Night time walk

body: This is a real gem of a place. A really worthy and interesting conservation project. Apart from all the trees and plants, there is a lot of wild life. I did not stay long enough in Dambulla to do a night safari with the hope of seeing the loris. However, my daytime walking safari, with the Manager, Mr. Amerasinghe was most informative, and in addition to the flora, we were lucky enough to see some wonderful wild animals, not least wonderful bird life and a giant squirrel. Entry to the Arboretum is free although there are suggested donations for the daytime and night time safaris
title: A 'Must See' near Dambulla

body: With a few of my friends, I stayed one night at Popham's Arboretum. It was a very nice experience. it was nice waking up to the sounds of the birds. The people there were very friendly and truly supportive. Would love to go back again.
title: A great experience surrounded by nature!

body: We went there during the day time and at the moment there were no guide and we were asked to go in, there were arrows colored in different colors to make our way easier we followed pink route and we got lost in the middle, as the arrows were missing. Finally we came backwards in the same route. I think it wil be better if you go with a tour. For a local they charged 250 LKR. Its worth visiting this place and specially ask for a guide if not it wont be that worth.
title: Good for nature lovers

body: Very disappointing the way the guide treated us. We had a very nice intro from another guide who explained us about the entire project (very nice preservation plan). We were supposed to walk 1 / 1 and a half hour but the guide after only 30 minutes took us back with no reason. He said that we saw already 3 loris and that was enough. Of course they charged the entire price (1500LKR) which was supposed to be for more than one hour. Won’t be back
title: Not happy

body: Yesterday we visited Popham's Arboretum for a night walk and had a great expirience. The naturalist (Poorna) was brilliant! He was very knowledgeable and managed to accommodate us on short notice, however please do phone them well ahead for the night walk. We managed to see 2 amazing grey slender loris, a fishing cat, mouse and spotted deers and others. The arboretum is run on donations and we found it great value for money.
title: Night Walk

body: Great night tour by Poorna to see the wild Loris - we even saw a baby! We also walked around before it got dark and saw a Giant Squirrel. Very good
title: Good tour

body: Office wasn’t occupied so we had to call a number which wasn’t answered first.Sign on entrance says there is a donation to do for the safari (recommend 1500 LSR for 1-1.5h tour). We had to pay 3500 LSR for two people and got only 45 minutes of walk through the Arboretum. Furthermore guide didn’t speak any English so it was just a walk with two short stops watching the Loris trying to escape from the flashlight. At least we saw two Loris, but for the price I wouldn’t recommend at all.
title: Expensive Walk

body: We went late afternoon for Loris watching and wow was it worth it ! We were welcomed with a cup of tea and a very warm welcome of the tame baby owl who was very sweet. Poorna the enthusiastic arboretum specialist gave us first a very interesting explanation about the arboretum and Loris, his knowledge is amazing! We then went out to find the Loris as soon as it was dark, Poorna gave us head torches and we saw 3 Loris and a baby Loris within 20minutes!We can highly recommend a visit !
title: Loris watching

body: We were accompanied by Poorna who was incharge of this place.He had a sound knowledge of history of arboretum,it's founder,the types of plants & the kind of nocturnal animals present at this wonderful place.Our night walk lasted around 1 hour & we had 3 Loris sightings.Their charge for the night walk was also reasonable I must mention.We also saw 2 mouse deer as well.
title: Night walk to see Loris

body: The eco garden was intiated and nurched by Mr Poperm a german expatriate who lived in Sri Lanka in early 70's and was his property and residence. A pioneer eco devoloper who started growing hardwood,medicinal trees,and friut orchard with some watwr features as well.to attract a variety of bird species and indigenous animals, which over the years has developed into a wonderful bird and animal heaven. It is permitted to visit the garden and there night visits to spot some species like the oriel, otto and fishing cat.
title: Eco Bio Diversified garden.

body: My guide arranged a guided night walk for me . The young warden was very well informed and gave a clear and concise explanation of the work at the arboretum . Equipped with a red light head torch we had 4 views of the Grey Slender-toed Loris , Ring-tailed and Pam Civets , young Spotted Deer and sleeping , White-browed Bulbul and Tailor bird .
title: Exciting night walk

body: The caretaker is a lovely man with loads of knowledge and keen sense of history. I would have loved to see the lorises but didnt visit at night when they are active. Enjoy a quiet walk through the forest and sample the natural medicinal treats.
title: Well worth a visit

body: Amazing chance to learn about and observe some very special animals including grey loris, spotted deer, mouse deer, vampire bats, giant squirrels and owls.
title: Amazing wildlife trail

body: This place is now run as a centre for Sri Lankan children's education on the flora and fauna of this wonderful island. To us it was just marvellous to think that Sam Popham was still there as recently as 1999 and gave over his life's work to the country.Our guide while we were there had actually worked there since he was a small boy.
title: A real education

body: We had an amazing tour of the abboretum with Jayantha who is so knowledgeable of all the different species here and has a true passion for the work he does, it was very inspiring to see. Would definitely recommend you to come and visit to see and learn about the stunning wildlife here.
title: Great experience

body: The place is a really hidden gem. Few minutes from Dambulla. The guide is really kind an shows what you want to see. There are trees, animals and many more.
title: Awesome place, nice guiding

body: Nothing exceptional to write home about except for the exorbitantcharges. You are better off with a Safari to the Hurulu Eco Park just 2 kms away from Habarana Junction.
title: No value for money

body: We visited Pophams Arboretum at 7pm. We had a great experience we saw loris, fireflys, deer and birds. The guides are knowledgeable and great at spotting animals. Would recommend!
title: Great experience

body: We had no idea that we had to make a booking and just decided to turn up one night for a night safari. Luckily after calling the manager he kindly arranged someone to come out for us. The safari was great we saw Loris, mouse dear, spotted dear and birds. I would definitely recommend this. Make sure you wear sneakers as you are walking through the forest in the dark. We paid 1500 R each however were asked for a 500R donation each as well which was not put on our receipt. I do think a donation should be at your discretion with an amount you feel comfortable with not requested.
title: Great night walk, make sure you book!

body: Held by nature enthusiasts, this place is ideal for a beautiful walk in the middle of various trees and plants.
title: Wonderfull

body: Ok so my friend and I made the mistake of not booking, but we were very lucky that we called in time for them to organise a guide for a night tour. Our student guide was great, we saw 4 or 5 Lorises, mouse dear, spotted dear, spiders, termite mounds, sleeping birds, fire flies. It was very interesting. And yes you have to pay a fee. after all it is a guided tour on private land but we happily paid the 2000Rupee per person which includes a tip for the guide. Covered shoes are a must. There are lots of loose tree roots, rocks and black ants that like to bite so keep your feet covered.
title: Don’t forget to book

body: We had a wonderful night safari and were lucky enough to spot two slow lorises and a porcupine! The naturalist guide was very enthusiastic and knew how to give the tour with great energy. We also stayed for a night and the room is quite basic - comparable to camping. A nice and quiet place surrounded by great nature.
title: Great night tour with enthusiastic naturalist

body: This place is a complete rip off! It used to be 250 rps each. Why I have to pay at all for a walk in the forest is a mystery, but ok 250rps is acceptable. We arrived 1 hour before closing and wanted a little stroll. We were taken into the office and greeted with talk of a tour guide etc which we politely declined, saying we just wanted a little walk. The park warden then told us we had to pay a "donation" of 2000 rps. We offered him a donation of 1000 rps (already extortionate!), to which he got very angry and started shouting at us. We obviously left immediately, not without trying to explain the concept of donation! We are from the New Forest in the UK and have visited many wonderful forests all over the world and have never had to pay to go for a walk in the woods! The park warden was greedy and angry when we refused to pay that much, trying to justify his price with talk of 'maintanence work'. Please don't bother going here. On our walk back to our hotel we saw a lake with many beautiful birds and flowers. There's enough wildlife with out being ripped off just because you're a tourist.
title: Terrible experience

body: We did a nightwalk with a student and an older guide in the forest and we were only 4 people joining the tour which was perfect for us. In total we paid 2000 Rupees per person. The walk was very interesting and we got very lucky in terms of animal sightings! We saw mouse deer, a couple of loris‘s, fire flies and also sleeping butterflies and birds! It was so lovely to see a sleeping bird so close! It’s better to wear some sneakers because there is often some quick running involved when there is a loris spotted. It was amazing how these two guides spotted the animals in complete darkness! The younger guide really wanted to make sure we feel happy about the tour which felt a little strange to us. But nevertheless they did a great job and it was totally worth a visit a we highly recommend it!
title: interesting nightwalk

body: Please go to this peaceful arboretum in Dambulla. It was one of the highlights from our Honeymoon. We took the long walk around the arboretum and saw dear, birds, monitors, squirrels and beautiful flora. Very special.
title: Beautiful, educational and peaceful

body: We visited here at midday and walked around the green trail seeing mostly plants , birds and butterflies. Poorna Tharaka, a student, gave us a good introductory talk and showed us some interesting medicinal plants. He took us to a small brick building where he stone a torch to reveal some vampire bats! Amazing.He does night tours where you can see loris and there are also early morning bird walks.It’s a lovely place to visit.
title: Great place for wildlife

body: We had a great visit to the arboretum. We had a daytime guided tour of the forest which was very enjoyable and informative. The forest is beautiful with many trails you can follow. We also went for an evening guided tour to look for the slender loris. A naturalist took us round and we were lucky enough to see the loris, mouse deer and lots of fireflies. It was a completely different experience walking through the forest at night.
title: Arboretum visit

body: Had an amazing night walk in the arboretum. We were fortunate enough to see 3 slender lorises, a civet cat, numerous mouse deer and spotted deer and some incredible birds!! The guides are extremely talented at spotting lorises and other animals and have a wealth of information. This was an incredible highlight for us and something we'll never forget. Mr Jayantha is extremely welcoming and happy to explain in great detail about the various fauna in the area. Visitors should be comfortable with night walking :)
title: Incredible slender loris tour

body: Had a very interesting night trek in the Arberatom with Mr Jayantha & Jemis who were ever so talented in spotting loris & other animals. It’s unbelievable how they spot the Loris! We were able to spot 3 of them during the tour. We also saw deer, wild cat, crocodile gecko etc. Wish we came during day light to enjoy the jungle.It’s amazing to see how dedicated & committed Mr Jayantha is towards this place and he is so knowledgeable as well. There are 2 rooms available if anyone wishes to stay over.
title: Loris tour- Great!

body: Good place for nature trails as well as to study about different variety of plants & many species of birds, spiders, mammals, etc.. Mr. Amarasinghe does a great job to protect the nature. Thanks to him, we learnt a lot. Also, our 04 year old daughter loved to be in the nature which was a good experience for her. After the trek, nice to had a chat while tasting a tea which he offered.
title: Good place for nature trails as well as to study about different variety of plants

body: We visited in February this year and had a wonderful time. Mr Amarasinghe took us round, explaining in depth about the various flora and fauna. We wanted to do a night walk, but unfortunately were limited on time. We were very fortunate to see a mouse deer in the daytime, which is uncommon apparently. Would definitely recommend visiting, it's a very unique experience that needs tourist support. We would love to come back to Sri Lanka one day, and will definitely return and hopefully do a night walk!
title: Amazing Visit

body: We enjoyed a wonderful Arboretum tour with Jayantha the manager. A “one off” in Sri Lanka. Needs supporting by tourists so preservation of unique trees can be assured. We’ll definitely come back for the evening Loris Tour at sunset.
title: Amazing Wildlife

body: We had a fantastic night walk with Poorna Tharaka! Thank you very much for showing us the place, some Loris and the mouse deers.We would really recomend it to everyone. :-)Please do not wonder about the missing lights at the entrance. Just walk in and follow the path to the office. The boys are a bit hidden...Thank you very very much!
title: Fantastic night walk

body: We did a night walk from 7pm for the price of 1500 rupees per person. If your goal is to spot the loris in the wild then its definitely worth the short amount of time and little money you will spend, as the guide is very good at finding them and also any other animals such as the very cute mouse deer. Unfortunately I can't say that we learnt very much as the night guides English was quite limited, which is a shame as he had great enthusiasm and is studying a related course at university.
title: Night walk

body: Just did a short walkaround under the tutelage of quite a competent ranger who, despite the fact that he was rather ill, took the time to do a short walk with us.
title: Nice colonial garden

body: Please please go visit this wonderful place. We went twice, once during the day and once for a night tour to see the Loris - and we did!!!! Mr Jayarantha went with us both times and we have become great friends. Thank you Mr. Jayarantha!!! And thank you Mr. Popham.
title: Best part of our Sri Lanka trip

body: We went to the arboretum as it sounded like a intriguing place for a relaxing exploration of local flora and fauna.We were met by the curator who gave us a personal tour of the arboretum with a fascinating incite into its history and challenges. We couldn’t help but be moved by his passion.We chose to go in the afternoon, however, it turns out that evening or early morning are the best times to see the wildlife.It is certainly worth planning a visit.
title: Fascinating place

body: Was an interesting experience, well worth the 10 USD charge, however instructions could be a little more clear and politely stated. We managed to see 3 slender Loris, 1 mouse dear, a sleeping Warbler and some spotted dear, plus a terrapin in an old water tank (I suspect he's trapped there.)
title: Slender Loris Safari

body: We stayed here for one night and it was lovely. The curator is very knowledgable and passionate about local plant and animal species and the arboretum. We were also able to go on a night tour with the naturalist and saw some mouse deer and spotted deer, a loris, a babbler bird, some turtles, a civet cat and a baby rabbit. The next morning we were able to walk around the property and spotted some monkeys too. Perfect for travellers who love nature, comfortable but no-frills accommodation and genuine people. The indoor/outdoor shower was beautifully executed. We would definitely recommend Popham's!
title: Stunning location!

body: The arboretum was very different from the usual exotic and luxurious Sri Lankan foliage. The very knowledgeable resident guide explained all the unusual plants, their provenance and their purpose as we walked around. It would have been good to do a night time tour of the arboretum, hopefully to see the slender loris and other unusual nocturnal creatures - another time perhaps. However we did get to see a colony of tiny bats who were not fazed by our presence. The tour ended in the cottage with a cup of delicious green tea while our guide patiently fielded lots of questions.
title: Very different and educational

body: We booked a triple room to stay here overnight. The plan was to do a night walk on arrival and an early morning walk next day before check out. The manager was very helpful in explaining and arranging by email.We arrived later than expected on Sri Lankan new year night, and were told the night walk was done at 7pm, and since it was 8:30, it was too late. However, as I said the kids were really looking forward to it, the guide agreed to do an hour of walk but warned us that the chances of seeing Loris were much lower at this time of the night as the nocturnal animals now were active and moving about. Anyway, we decided to take the chance. Walking in the dark jungle tracks was good, although occasionally you've got to mind low branches etc. The animals were very difficult to see, and we ended up seeing a wildcat very fleetingly, and 3 sleeping birds near the accommodation block. So, one can conclude that the night walk was a disappointment, but it was us who had arrived late and the guide did his best despite obviously wanting to go home for new year, so he deserves a special thanks. There are suggested donation amounts for guided walks that help with conservation efforts.I did a short unguided morning walk, again birds were difficult to see and photograph but there were lovely birdsongs. I recorded audio on my phone instead of trying to take pictures. 4 walks of varying lengths are clearly signposted through acres of trees and woodland.The room was great bargain, clean with a decent bath, cold shower. Perfect for a warm jungle stay. No a/c but a pedestal fan was enough for us.They only provide tea in the morning, they cannot provide breakfast etc as they are primarily a research and conservation center with small number of gardening staff at hand. There is a small office, where you can learn more on local flora fauna through posters. My only suggestion to the management would be to clearly inform the visitors that the night walk is best done around 7pm, otherwise sightings are rare. I've been to many night walks in India even much later and seen wildlife so I didn't think timings would be an issue and therefore did not try to get there earlier to my regret.
title: Great experience in natural surroundings

body: A unique magic place in the world, amazing staff and very warm welcome for everyone. I definitely recommend to visit! Thank you for accommodate us and for the great service provided.
title: Simply amazing

body: We did a night time visit to the Arboretum specifically to spot slender loris. During the 90 minutes there were two brief encounters. Unfortunately once they spotted a loris our guides made a lot of noise and shone strong torch lights at the loris. Unsurprisingly the loris beat a hasty retreat. You need to be sure footed and watch out for overhead branches across the path. Although our tour company had prepaid we were charged 1500 rp each at the end of the night. Only $24 so we did not make a big issue of it. Subsequently our tour company refunded this charge.We wouldn’t bother to revisit. As we found out later there are several public areas around Habarana where loris can be freely viewed at night.
title: Night Time Visit

body: A truly unique, beautiful and friendly place that should be on everyone's list to visit. I spent a month at the Arboretum during the summer of 2017 and would happily go there for another month if I had the money!I was blown away by two things:The Wildlife - We went on many day time and night time safaris and during these walks we saw some incredible wildlife, from birds of paradise through to Slender Loris. It was amazing to see a regenerated area of forest that was home to so many endangered and endemic species.The Staff - Jayantha and his team are amazing. Their knowledge about the arboretum and it's inhabitants was endless. They were eager for us to learn and were incredibly accommodating throughout the whole month. The respect they also had for the environment of the animals that lived there made their wildlife safaris even more special. I highly recommend this place to anyone and really hope to visit again in the future.
title: An Incredibly Special and Unique Place - Rich with wildlife

body: What a fantastic and interesting place to visit! I had the pleasure of staying at the Arboretum last summer while on a trip with Falmouth University and fell in love with the woodland. Learning about it's history, the trees and the animals like the Grey Slender Loris was hugely exciting and the curator Jayantha is more than happy to spend as much time with you as you need. Mr Popham must have been a fascinating man and what achieved is incredible! A thoroughly recommended attraction for education and for cleansing the soul!
title: Tranquil and educational

body: Visiting the Arboretum I was astounded by the variety the 36 acres contained. I got to see three species of Kingfisher including the dwarf kingfisher during a morning walk along the trails as well as many other bird species. On a night walk I got to see a grey slender loris, palm civet and mouse deer. I want to go back and would recommend to anybody visiting Dambulla!
title: Incredible!

body: Me and a group of other students (Project Loris) spent five weeks here over summer researching and photographing the wildlife, it was amazing! Definitly a hidden gem, the arboretum deserves far more visitors than it seems to currently be getting.The staff and caretakers are friendly, informative and very hard working always going out of their way to accommodate you.If you love natural history it's a no brainer going during the day but I strongly recommend joining for one of the night walks. A host of rarely seen nocturnal critters come out and with some expert guidance, and maybe a decent red light head torch, you could glimpse the Arboretums star attraction, the endangered Slender Loris.The Arboretum seems to stay open largely thanks to donations so it's worth spending time with people like Jayantha to find out why the Arboretum is important and to learn about the wildlife there.
title: Great wildlife, great people, great place

body: I spent an amazing month last year as part of a Falmouth University expedition from the UK living, photographing and assisting research within the aboretum. Jayantha and his team were incredibly kind, knowledgable and welcoming, and would do anything to help our work and to educate us on the ecology of the aboretum and its wildlife.I would highly reccomend visiting this hidden gem of Sri Lanka, as there are hundreds of beautiful species, ranging from extremely rare tree species, mammals, reptiles, birds and invertebretes. A naturalists paradise, or anyone who loves to get outside. All the trails are accessable to all and easy to walk on, not at all strenuous. An incredible aboretum which needs protecting for future generations - If you're in the area make sure to visit, the staff are some of the most humble and knowledgable people I've ever met, and I can't wait to be back again.
title: Inspiring people, immensely biodiverse aboretum

body: We had a very enjoyable time walking through the arboretum with the caretaker, Jayantha. He is passionate about conserving the 36 acres, which he has cared for since 1994 when Sam Popham moved back to the UK. We visited mid-afternoon (not the best time for wildlife viewing) and saw Jungle Fowl, a tortoise and several birds and butterflies. Jayantha is extremely knowledge of the flora and fauna of the Arboretum and he shared several stories of medicinal plants and herbs. With no government funding, it is well worth the donation. Highly recommended to get away from the temples and stroll under the shade of trees, many of which are no longer found in the dry zone except here because of their commitment to conservation.
title: Interesting and important

body: Went for a night walk along with the manager of the guest house I was staying at. Me and the other person doing the walk that night were allocated a non-English speaking guide, which meant the guesthouse manager would translate what he could. Animals wise, spotted various species, but unfortunately the lack of any information in regards to animals or plants was a big let down
title: Quiet nightwalk

body: I visited the arboretum with a friend and our guide. We had a interesting walk with Mr. J. Amerasinghe who is passionate about the place and runs it almost single handed. He has great knowledge of the plants and wildlife and cares deeply for the arboretum. His knowledge and his stories about the arboretum's creation to the current day were fascinating. We also had an evening (prearranged) walk to try and see the nocturnal Loris that live in the park but didn't see any.
title: Extremely interesting

body: Many walking paths are available covering the whole area . very peaceful place to visit freely. Animals are also there. Night visits are also available as I heard. Worth a visit.
title: Peaceful knowledgable place to visit

body: Mr. J. Is the manager, guide, and trained botanist. And this little arboretum is teaming with local flora and fauna. It's a very relaxing 1-2 hours of walking and learning about the local environment. Very peaceful place and a nice change from the other local activities. I would return.
title: Wonderful walk

body: We saw the arboretum in the Rough Guide and thought it would make a change from yet another temple. So glad we did. It was a haven of peace (we were the only people there) and the guide was so informative about the plants and their medicinal effects. If you fancy a change from the temples, it's definitely worth a visit.
title: A peaceful change from more temples

body: Popham's Arboretum is a short distance out of the centre of Dambulla on the Kandalama Road. Basically it is an arboretum of native trees and plants with signposted walks through the area. One can be accompanied by a guide or wander through unaccompanied. It costs 1000 rupees per person to take the walks which we thought was a little on the steep side for what it is but you get peace, tranquility and an understanding of native flora and fauna. The day we went it was unfortunately raining so we did not complete the walks but we saw enough to know that we would return and that it is a place worth visiting if you are nature lovers. They have a supply of wellington boots if you don't have appropriate footwear and there are toilets.
title: Very interesting collection of trees and nice walk

body: Mr. J. Amerasinghe, arboretum director, personally identified the trees, birds and plants as we walked the woodland trails. He related the history of how the arboretum came to be established as a preserve for endemic species, and also mentioned the challenge of maintaining a natural reserve in this decade of development. We visited in the afternoon so did not see the lorises, which can be spotted on an evening walk. We arrived by tuk tuk after touring the caves and Dambulla museum. Late afternoon was the perfect time to see birds, and the weather was pleasant.
title: Native trees and trails, with bonus of medicinal herbs, made guided walk in the Popham Arboretum fascinating.

body: Nice staff. 1000 rupees enters for adults was a bit pricey. But it's ok. You can have a guide as part of the fee if you like else can follow a guided path of markers on your own. We followed the yellow trail. 60 odd markers which took circa 40 mins to walk. It's all tree so no colour. Saw no animals but saw deer prints so they are around. Very close to dambulla.get the tuk tuk driver to wait as don't think it gets too many visitors and you may get stranded.
title: Good way to kill an afternoon

body: Since we're nature enthusiasts, we really enjoyed this peaceful haven just outside of Dambulla, mostly thanks to the knowledgeable and sweet curator who took the time to show us around the leafy property, filled with local flora. Shame we coudn't stay for the evening loris search, but one always needs to leave stuff for the next visit.
title: Well-spent couple of hours

body: This is an amazing place to visit. We had an excellent tour with the curator of this beautiful woodland full of indigenous plants. The evening tours are well worth doing too for birdwatching. If you're in the Dambulla area, and have a couple of hours free, I really recommend it.
title: A really interesting tour.

body: Really enjoyed our guided tour around by Jayanth. His enthusiasm and commitment to maintaining and developing this indigenous woodland is impressive and inspiring. If you have any interest in horticulture its a must do and is a nice contrast to the more formal gardens in Sri Lanka (which are also good to visit). If you are visiting Dambulla Caves its worth the extra effort to go here as well.
title: This is a interesting place to spend a couple of hours

body: Take the time to visit this indigenous woodland. An evening tour is recommended although we took ours during the day with the very knowledgable Jayantha who now runs it on behalf of Sam Popham. It’s a truly peaceful haven and makes an excellent break from the busier, religious sites. You can ring ahead.
title: Well worth a visit

body: We read about this place in our guidebook as a place worth visiting if your in Dambulla and it definitely was. We called to book an evening tour on the same day without problem. Our great guides Poorna Tharaka and Rathnasiri took us out on a 1,5 hour walk to spot animals in the dark. We got to see loris, two types of deer, a wild cat, birds and frogs.
title: Lovely evening tour

body: We was visiting night part of this garden/forest. Very interesting to found animals at night like that also the guide gave us an information we was interested in. A lot of different plants and trees. Also good for kids. Easy to get to.and realy nice place to visit when you are in Dambulla. Many thanks!
title: House of the loris

body: We did the the night time walk to see the grey slender loris, and it was utterly magical. With two guides we walked through the arboretum, past sleeping butterflies and a dozing hornbill. The guides were brilliant, and soon spotted a pair of Loris in the tree tops. Amazing to see these tiny creatures. We were lucky enough to then see three more in another tree. We also saw a number of different insects, some bats and a civet cat. It was a great experience and comes highly recommended.
title: A magical night time walk

body: We went on the day tour AND the night tour and really enjoyed this glimpse into Sri Lankan nature and wildlife. Butterflies, insects, slender loris, bats, birds, snakes, mouse deer can all be seen in their natural habitats, as well as dozens of plants & trees. It's a place of education and research and there is a respect for the natural environment here. We turned up on the day without booking anything and had the pleasure of meeting Poorna who became our guide. He is a bright, educated, and interesting young man who is studying horticulture and has a passion for the environment he lives in. He's a real credit to the arboretum- we certainly learned a lot from him! Quick note - if you do the night tour expect to use a lot energy! You will be walking in the pitch black in the forest with only a few torches to light the way. It's exciting and memorable (especially as we saw three slender loris!), but be careful if you are tired or don't the like idea of walking in the woods in the dark.
title: Educational nature

body: We had a very different evening in Sri Lanka as our guide walked us through the forest in the pitch black looking for night time creatures. The most elusive being the adorable Lorus which we all searched for and finally found ! Hearing about how it all started and the amount of work they put in was quite amazing. Certainly worth a visit while you're over here.
title: Night watch

body: This is the only dry zone arboretum in Sri Lanka, established over 50 years ago by a british sailor. Sadly he was educated at Eton and sadly like one of prime minister he separated himself from the Europe and settled there for a long time until retirement when he returned to UK.Here was a land scared by cut trees including native trees such as palm. He established the arboretum and now after almost 650 years it is flourishing. It a marvelous place to see tons of butter flies, unusual and almost histori trees , bats and many other small birds including a rare giant squirrels.The current director, a native Sri Lanka has continued to improve on it and it loos great.You would be advised to visit for a morning or afternoon. It is in close proximity of Dumballa.Sadly it is not supported by the government and the project is dependent on visitors and donations.I likes most the rare buts in the old shed and massive formations of butterflies in the late afternoon.
title: Te IFS Popham Arboretum

body: Dedicating your life to nature,you will be always a winner.A great place to get a full idea of Sri Lanka's wildlife and beautiful plants it has.A well educated guide who has a huge amount of information and knowledge about nature,birds,animals and plants especially medical ones, guided us through the woods and provided us with unique information about the plants and animals there.Thanks a lot for giving us this opportunity to discover true Sri Lankan wildlife.Alsuhaibany Family
title: A piece of paradise

body: The Arboretum, is full of rare trees, an ancient ebony and a vast array of exotic birds, lizards, butterflys and of course the Grey Slender Loris (an endemic species, worthy of support). The knowledgeable staff are keen to show you around and explain the now famous "Poppham method". Well worth the donation, the Loris walk in the evening is an exlperience nt to be missed and is incredible value.Please go and support this oasis of biodiversity, you won't be dissapointed.
title: A hidden gem, full of unexpected treasures.

body: I would recommend the arboretum to anyone who is visiting! A true sanctuary for wildlife in Dambulla! In the day you will see many birds, reptiles, insects and primates! In the evening, I often saw ring-tiled civets, spotted deer, common palm civets and of course the slender loris! I visited the arboretum many times during my stay in Dambulla and we saw atleast one loris on every night walk!
title: Full of diversity & the place to see slender loris!

body: It's not easy to get to this place, largely because it's known by a completely different name to locals (Suddage Waththe....which kinda translates as "white guy's place"). We did not manage to call ahead but fortunately the guy in charge was right there. He took us around the arboretum for an extensive tour with great explanations of the history and mission of the place. Granted, I'm a total botany nerd, so maybe it's not everyone's cup of tea, but I was in heaven. This is a great effort to recreate native Sri Lankan forest, and should be supported.
title: Fantastic

body: We went here based on the information in a few years old Rough Guide book that the entrance is 250 Rs / person. However after we went in, we were asked for a "donation" of 1000 Rs / person. If it really is donation, then it should be up to people how much they want to give and AFTER the visit. However after taking the ride with tuk tuk we decided to pay it and see what is there. Honestly, it is just a forrest with some marked paths, now after some more travelling in Sri Lanka I would not recommend this, there are much better places for free.And one more comment to the owners - if you want to charge for entrance, please, call it an entrance fee as normal person would do and don't play stupid games with "donation". And put the sign at the entrance with fees. Now it gives an impression a "donation" goes to the pocket of the person "selling" it.
title: Overprized

body: This delightful Arboretum is a wonderful place to cool down after climbing rocks to hillside Temples and Fortresses in the area. One of those very special places born of the dedication of a few caring souls, the Arboretum is the result of one man's vision- Sam Popham, a British expat living in Sri Lanka for over 50 years- and the loving custodial care of another, Jayantha Amarasinghe.Special specimens such as a 200 year old Ebony tree, and a thriving and developing ecosystem in the Arboretum, make it a place to enjoy a shady afternoon- and if you are very lucky, you may be able to share a cup of tea and a chat with Mr Amarasinghe himself!Highly reccomend this!
title: Wonderful hidden treasure!

body: The building at the arboretum was designed by Geoffrey Bawa Srilanka's famous architect. We went there late in the evening & saw false vampire bats, giant sqirrels & a nesting nightjar amongst others. We did the Loris walk & glimpsed one fleetinglyPrasanna was there to help us round & that itself was a bonusTo experience the various trees try & get there early-there is plenty of shade within the aboretum
title: Host of various trees as expected & plenty of birds

body: I always enjoy night tours because there is always an air of mystery when walking around a forest at night, with the potential of seeing wildlife not seen during the daylight hours. Pop ham's Arboretum didn't disappoint. The manager/tour guide was very accommodating, especially given the fact that we made last minute reservations. Unfortunately we only got a fleeting glimpse of a slender loris or a pangolin, but we did get to see mouse deer. The hike is reasonably priced and fits perfectly after a visit to Sigirya for the day.
title: Chance to see Slender Loris

body: We had read wonderful reviews about this place and decided to check it out one rainy afternoon. Mr. Jayantha Amarsinghe provided us with some insights into the history and purpose of the place. We took the yellow trail which took us 2 hours to complete. We saw quite a number of birds including the jungle fowl, the Asian Paradise Flycatcher, black headed bulbul etc. We knew that we had to make a donation but we were taken aback when we were presented with a receipt showing a predetermined amount. Maybe they should just have tickets instead of calling it a donation and making it mandatory. Overall, a hidden gem in Dambulla.
title: Wonderful trail, mandatory donation.

body: It is a wonderful place to relax and cool down after the arduous climb to the rock paintings and the temple. Take a picnic and enjoy the peace.
title: A Haven From The Heat

body: Popham's Arboretum is a very peaceful and beautiful place! We spent a night in one of the rooms. Simple but clean! We got some tea when we arrived and could observe some Sri Lanka Jungle Fowl! We also walked one of the very nice and well marked trails. It's a very nice and wild forest! After sunset we made the night safari and saw bats, one lori and two mouse deers!! The staff is very friendly and helps you out with everything you need! We really liked this place and enjoyed our stay!
title: Wonderful Place for Nature Lovers

body: We arrived early afternoon and were greeted by Mr J Amarasinghe, the curator of the arboretum. He is an encyclopedia of knowledge about the plants and animals within this green and quiet haven. He gave us samples of leaves to taste or smell, and explained the medicinal properties of the flora. He knew which plants were endangered and which were the only left in Sri Lanka. His respect for the land and its natural bounty deserves honor by supporting his work. By all means, go.
title: Nature walk

body: We spent an hour wandering the nature trail, viewing the birds and butterflies on the trail. In some of the outbuildings there are also several species of bats to view, including false vampire bats!We visited in the afternoon, but the best time to visit is apparently in the morning. You can also do a slow Loris safari at sunset where you may see Slow Loris. This costs 1500 rupees.We left a donation to contribute towards the upkeep of the reserve.
title: A Relaxing hour or so

body: Popham's Arboretum is a marvellous place to visit if you like proper nature and not packaged stuff more akin to a zoo or wildlife park. The staff are few but dedicated and because it has quiet times they are happy to engage at length with you. When I visited I heard about the background, the possible wildlife around and before I set off on one of the trails I was taken to see both 'vampire' bats (they are not) and horseshoe bats. Both were roosting in different locations and it was wonderful to get up close to see them. You have a choice of trails which intersect and they are very well marked. I took the pink one and at strolling pace with many stop offs to listen and observe it took me around 2 hours. I saw very little, in part due to a few other noisy vistors who maybe thought it was a place to stroll and chat loudly, but also jbecause heading for midday the birds and wildlife are sensibly keeping in the shade. I heard mutliple calls, and also much movement in the bush. There were a lot of butterflies everywhere. I did see many yellow billed babbler, and one male Asian Paradise kFlycatcher which as usual showed confidently. Be warned the trails are not for people unsteady on their feet and at times the stream crossings are a balancing act. I found it a superb visit and am planning to go back to meet with the staff for a dawn walk before I depart the area.
title: Wonderful

body: My partner and I spent a couple of hours at the Arboretum although could have spent longer. The manager Mr Jayantha Amerasinghe took us on a walk through the site and provided us with fascinating information about Popham, the site, history, plants and wildlife. If you are interested in nature then a visit is thoroughly recommended. The arboretum was just a few km from Dambula and easily managable in a Tuktuk. We had ours wait for us, and in the end the driver followed round and also seemed to enjoy the tour, having never originally heard of the arboretum.Dusk is a recommended time to go to see the wildlife, and you can book a guided walk, but we turned up unnanounced which seemd not to be any issue.
title: Relased wooded Sri Lankan nature trails

body: I only visited for an evening but could easily have stayed a few days. There is a lot of wildlife in a small area here, including some very rare and unusual stuff. The site is run by the very helpful Mr Jayantha Amarasinghe who will show you some photos and tell you about the site, before leading you on a night walk through the trails. There is a good chance for slender loris here although I was unlucky. Our guide did however find a rusty spotted cat. Birding is also supposed to be very good during the day and a few species of bats can be found. The site is maintained by donations and visitors fees so do call in if you're in the area!
title: Fantastic place to visit if you are into wildlife

body: We visited Popham's Arboretum for a very special two hours at dusk. Mr Jayantha, the manager, is a passionate and knowledgeable advocate for this unique conservation project. He generously made time to guide us around, showing us medicinal trees and shrubs, birds, bats, moths and geckos. After dark, I was lucky indeed to see a slender loris, high up in the branches and gazing calmly down at us with its huge nocturnal eyes. This rare place is a real treasure, and needs all the support it can get.
title: Unique and wonderful little nature oasis

body: We made a stop at Sam Popham's Arboretum on our way to Habarana and we're so glad we included it in our itinerary. We started the trail at around 10 am and took around 1.5 hours to complete it. There are 4 different trails and we followed the one sign posted by the yellow tags. It was a beautiful walk and although it was close to noon, the weather was really pleasant because the forest was so dense and the canopies didn't allow most of the sunlight to reach the ground level. The trail wasn't difficult and it was well sign posted so there is zero chance of getting lost. We spotted monitor lizards, giant squirrels and different bird flocks. The curator of the Arboretum, Mr Jayantha Amarasinghe is a very friendly gentleman who was very happy to share the story of the Arboretum with us. He is truly a 'guardian' of the forest. Sam Popham's Arboretum is a must-visit place in Sri Lanka!
title: One of the best nature trails!

body: We took the 7pm night tour for spotting slow loris. The usual owner of the arboretum was away on vacation, so we had a friendly chap who helped to cover duties, but who was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about wildlife.The main guide was an elder who has been at the arboretum for more than 30 years. He searches for slow loris using a red light, only switching the flashlight when one is found. We managed to see 2 slow lorises that night! Only 1500 rupees per person, but good to donate more to support the aborteum.
title: Fantastic slow loris spotting night tour

body: We spent a thoroughly interesting two hours with Jayantha, learning about the various indigenous trees and their uses, as well as learning something of the history of the arboretum. A real national treasure.This place is certainly worth a visit if you are interested in the natural world.
title: Popham Arboretum, Dambulla.

body: Stayed overnight when passing through Dambulla. THe place is basic but clean. Complete value for money though as charge is just for Room. Meals can be arranged from places nearby. The caretaker was very helpful, and we managed to see three Slender Loris. In the morning time there are lots of birds that fly through. Place has unique and rustic quality. If you have time drive around Kandalama lake and visit the ruins at Kaludiya Pokuna nearby.
title: Trip through Dambulla

body: Dropped by Sam Popham Arboretum, Sri Lanka last weekend. Filled the vehicle with sapling...excellent selection. Got some hard-to-find Gal siyambala, Weera, Kora Kaha, Burutha, Kaha Pethan, Bata Kirilla as well as the more popular Ehala, Welang, Hal milla...See you next time!
title: Always nice to come here

body: This is such a quaint little place part of a tree sanctuary where they are planting new trees all the time. The facilities are average but you're there more for what is outside your room rather than what is inside. The location is interesting and close to quite a few sites such as Dambulla Cave Temples and Minneriya National Park.Staff are very helpful, kind and friendly.However do not trust the arrows on the trees in the forest because some of them are wrong and could you get you lost as in the 'Blair Witch Project'. Ha ha! This happened to us on the morning we had to leave!
title: If you want to experience 'Secret Sri Lanka' stay here for a few nights!

body: We visit their and at the time of our visit only a helper is there He was helpful but not a good guide.So If you wants to visit please made a arrangement for guide.It's like worth of going a big land with so many plants and trees . If you get good explanation I think it's worth .For us it unfortunate.We have seen few bats and jungle fowl and also it's dry day .There was no rain for days .
title: Popham,s Arboretum ...

body: I visited in September 2016 with some friends from the Colombo area. We had a great time. The manager was very friendly, and took us on a few hikes through the arboretum. My favorite was a nighttime safari, during which I spotted a loris! Definitely a high point of my trip. Yes, the facilities are rustic, but that's the point! It's a great feeling getting away from the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoying the natural world. I would recommend this place to anyone who is looking for a rustic getaway in a beautiful natural setting.
title: Great time at the Popham Arboretum- Loris Included!

body: We visited Popham's Arboretum just as the sun was setting. We were shown by our knowledgeable and enthusiastic guide two colonies of bats, the Leaf Eared and then Fake Vampire. Then we headed into the forest once it was dark, with red filters over our torches so as not to disturb the Lorises. I don't know lots about these little primates but it was so exciting to spot their gleaming eyes in the darkness and to see one climbing quickly up a tree.We were also taught about the Popham's Method of protecting and encouraging native species of tree.A really good evening and an important conservation project.
title: Wonderful guided walk in this forest. Great place to see the rare Loris !

body: Surprising spot which we found in our travel pocket...24/7 open to visit. The very friendly guide gave us a nice tour over the property and was highly motivated to tell the story of this forest and the specials in it...We enjoyed the almost 2 hour tour...
title: Amazing

body: A wonderful afternoon in a wonderful place. The manager introduced us into this magical oasis, he guided us through this natural forest in the most nicely way. You learn a lot of interesting things about the history of the country and its nature.We recommend you to go with time to meet this lovely place, one of the best attractions of Dambulla.
title: Amazing

body: I enjoyed the 2 hours I spent here walking through the forest with the friendly and extremely knowledgable manager learning about the local flora and fauna. It was especially interesting to learn the medicinal uses for a lot of the plants. After going to a lot of overpriced tourist destinations, it was very refreshing to visit the arboretum. An added bonus was to see the Geoffry Bawa desgined house. I would love to come back some day and see the loris at night.
title: Visit this Arboretum to support a unique conservation project

body: A wonderful place with an excellent volunteer guide but not what I was expecting. The designated routes are not always easy to follow 'the monkeys turn the signs round', access across streams is not easy but well worth visiting. An interesting history and hopefully a future of doing important conservation work. Fun place for children to explore.
title: Unique experience

body: Jayantha is a knowledgeable guide for this forest / arboretum reserve at Dambulla. We loved our visit, especially the bats and the Loris.
title: Wonderful experience with nature

body: Really wonderful little arboretum in Sri Lanka. Our guide, who is also the manager was very passionate about the place and nature, which is always contagious and great to see. We did the night time walk/safari, and saw 3 loris (up fairly high), a baby spotted deer (up close) and 2 sleeping birds, also we got there a little early so we went to meet the resident bats before they went out for the night!If you love nature, wildlife and trees I don't think you will be unhappy spending a cup of hours here. Thumbs up from me! 🤗Tip - Wear long trousers, sleeves and sturdy boots. And Take a torch for the night time walk.
title: Night time walk - saw the Loris!

body: This is NOT just another spice garden. It is an inspirational piece of conservation undertaken by Sam Popham who cared about the future of our natural heritage. It has been continued by his long term assistant and friend and deserves all the support we can give it. To get most benefit DO make an appointment and be guided around the collection. You will be made most welcome. Go by Tuk Tuk from Dambullah.
title: Fascinating conservation project.

body: We had a great experience at the arboretum today! Mr. Amarasinghe gave us an educational and entertaining tour of the area. His knowledge of the flora and local environment are incredible. It was good to see environmental programs like his happening here. Our young children loved the easy walks and bats! The sip of tea was especially nice at the end of our visit!
title: Gem of a spot!

body: If you like birds and bats then it is very well worth paying a visit and following one of the very well signposted routes.
title: Great birds and small bats

body: Went on camping at Popham's Arboretum and stayed for one night. Awesome place to camping while enjoying the beauty of mother nature.
title: Nice Place to Camping

body: We visited here last summer. We had a great guided tour through the forest that made "nature conservation" to us a very real thing. Indeed it is difficult. The manager of the property does a great job in protecting the trees against the marble quarry nearby and the animals against poaching. In response to some other reviewer who complained: if you think it is expensive then at least the money goes to a good cause. But we didn't think it expensive.
title: You must love the trees

body: I have visited at Popham arboteum in an evening when I was coming from Matale. It is situated about 3Km from Dambulla in Kandalama road. We spent about 2 hours there and walking along well paved foot pathway was a nice experiance.This place is famous for Lorris viewing and you have to come in night time for it. But Rs 1500 for a person for Lorris viewing is bit expensive. Then you can spend a night there. They have a room for reasonable amount.There was no a knowledgeable person during my visit. The caretaker gave me a leaflet which explaining the history and evelution of the arboteum. Through entrance is free it is better donate some money.It is worth to visit there in your Dambulla visit.
title: Nice place to get relax

body: Very interesting tour of herb farm. I learnt a lot about the use of herbs here Bring some herbs and spices home, the best I have used.
title: Medicinal herb farm

body: ENG: A bit too expensive, but really nice! Absolutely recommend. Hint: when you're inside follow one of the colored signs for the path, or you will get lost very easily.ITA: Un po' troppo caro, ma molto carino! Raccomando assolutamente.
