title: Nice

body: It's great when you come across conservation works actually in situ, living in the Western world we are used to being asked to donate to such good causes but here you can see first hand the great work and enthusiasm to try to help remain and restore the endangered species of trees in the island.It is so uplifting to meet like minded people. Long may you continue and be able to carry on the great work you provide which is so needed. God bless you.
title: Wonderful place, please support this good good cause

body: This place was a surprising lovely little find when we had half a day to fill up. It wasn't on our agenda but really glad we found it. We did a lovely nature walk for a couple of hours, saw lots of beautiful butterflies. At the end we had a nice cup of tea with the manager in the mud house hut and saw all the old photos of Mr Popham and heard the special story of how it was set up years ago. Worth a visit if you are into nature.
title: Special place for nature lovers

body: We visited the IFS Popham Arboretum and Sanctuary earlier this year. It is a sanctuary for the tropical trees and for native wildlife. Many of the indigineous trees of Sri Lanka are becoming very rare. You can call here to schedule a day or night hike. Nights you might see slow lories. Mr. J. Amerasinghe is ambitious and generous in devoting himself to preserve the dry zone nature of Sri Lanka for future generations. They have removed the scrub brush and allowed many native tree species to flourish. In addition they have an education program for young Sri Lankans, and a tree nursery to increase rare tree populations in other places in Sri Lanka. You can see trees, medicinal plants, flowering plants, bats, squirrels, slow lories, birds, butterflies and dragonflies here. If you just want to have a lovely cool nature walk in Dambulla, or want to support such selfless and important endeavors and learn a great deal I urge you to visit!
title: An oasis for nature lovers and botanists in Sri Lanka

body: when you visit the Arboretum better be there by 6.00 am or after 7.00 pm to see loris, I think yellow trac is the best and it's the longest as well if lucky you will be able to see spotted deer,fishing cat as well
title: See slender loris

body: My husband and I stopped by after seeing the Dambulla Cave Temple. Jayantha who looks after the arboretum was just about the head home for the day but kindly extended his day so he could show us around. Come here if you want to enjoy an easy walk for an hour or two and have Jayantha enthusiastically guide you through to learn about the plants and their medicinal properties and spot some wildlife along the way. We unfortunately had come mid-afternoon and it had just rained so there was not as much bird life as there would be if we came in the early morning (6am) or late afternoon. However we did see bats, giant squirrels, a small lizard, butterflies, and a few colourful birds. Apparently there are loris and pangolins to see at night time tours so we will love to come back for that one day. Sam Popham has setup a wonderful educational arboretum and Jayantha's enthusiasm for keeping it alive is infectious. Even David Bellamy (a botanist / TV broadcaster whom I watched on TV as a kid) has been here. This place survives on donations alone so do make one as it is really a little gem! Thank you Jayantha for a wonderful afternoon tour - Post photos from the morning bird tours and evening loris/pangolin tours and the chance to stay overnight and I think you will get a good following! :)
title: Beautiful nature walk

body: Really lovely to get away from all the crowds and walk in the cool of the clearly marked paths. Saw some giant squirrels and some bats. The whole experience was soured by the usual extortionate expectation that the tourists are a walking ATM. I would not pay £10 for an hours walk in a park in England, so why I need to in Sri Lanka is beyond me. But you have taken a tuk tuk and the owner suggests this is a reasonable amount after a bit of buttering you up at the start. Another example of 'biting the hand that feeds you'. So if you are happy to spend 2000 rupees for 2 people to take an hours walk in some nice quiet woods then this is a great place to go.
title: Great garden, ridiculous 'donation' expected!

body: A wonderful way to spend a couple of hours whilst in Dambulla. We wandered through the arboretum photographing the various butterflies and birds we encountered whilst wandering through the natural dry forest (rains only falls on 90 days per year). There's also the opportunity to spot a loris if you arrange a night walk. The history and significance of Sam Popham's environmental regeneration methods are really interesting. Our guide was Mr Jayantha Amarasekara, who now runs the place. There's also the opportunity to spot a loris if you His English is perfect and his enthusiasm is infective. This place relies on donations, so please visit if you are in the area. It's only 6km out of Dambulla.
title: Serendipity in Dambulla - a great place to spend a few hours.

body: We nearly didn't go here but had a few hours to spare so gave them a call then took the 15 minute ride out from Dambulla. We were greeted by the wonderful Mr Amarasinghe. He explained how the arboretum had been started and showed us photos of the forest before and after it had been treated by the "Popham" method, gave us some literature to read later, then took us out into the forest for around an hour and a half. The walk wasn't just about the trees and plants, we saw bats, lizards, a giant squirrel, butterflies, deer footprints and much more! I cannot recommend this place highly enough, Mr Amarasinghe's enthusiasm is contagious and we had a wonderful time!
title: Do not miss this place!

body: We walked the yellow trail. (about 2 hours doing a lot of birding along the way) It is well signed and allows you to explore several different habitats. Along the way we saw a variety of interesting birds including: Black-headed Cuckooshrike, Jerdon'sand Golden-Fronted Leafbirds, Black-hooded orioles, Forest Wagtails, White-Browed Bulbul, several Asian Paradise Flycatchers, White-rumped Shama,Lotten's and Purple Rumped Sunbirds, and of course yellow-biked Babblers, Common Myna, and Spotted Doves. Truly a birding hotspot, especially in winter. No commercial pressure, just a donation to continue the educational mission and keep the land as a nature center into the future.
title: Great Birding Site

body: I have both visited and worked in several conservation and environmental activities in this location. It is a special destination but sometimes the management and ownership seems to be floating away from their main objective and purpose.I'd be very sad if I see Tourism has made damage to the place and they would loose their conservation aspect of the location.I would like the future visitors to keep this fact in their minds and concern about what could happen if they develop this location as a tourist destination?
title: Good Loris spotting place!
Mr. Popham's bride...
body: This special place is a bubble of peace and quiet for the trees and animals, ourselves included. The experience we had here was thoroughly enjoyable because of the serene environment, warm welcome, and the lovely walks trough this space.Every walk is a unique experience. Sometimes is a loris buffet, and sometimes its an orchestra of frogs! The expert eyes and the genuine passion of the people safeguarding this sanctuary will ensure that you will be enjoying the sights and sounds of the animals sharing the area.This arboretum is a very generous initiative and we hope that it will be around for many generations to come.

title: Perfect sanctuary for trees and wildlife
body: If you like wildlife and nature, then you must visit here. We arrived unannounced, but were warmly welcomed.An exceptionally knowledgeable and passionate student volunteer offered to guide us around the small, beautifully created arboretum. The trees were one thing, but the biodiversity and associated flora and fauna were another. Within minutes we spotted a giant squirrel, a kangaroo lizard and flocks of sunbirds. I would have missed them all, but our wonderful guide pointed them out to us patiently, lending his binoculars and showing us exactly what we were looking at in his guide books. My personal highlights were the black hooded oriole and the mouse deer, but there were many, many more. Meeting the manager sweeping paths along the way, we were taken for a detour to see some very special trees. This clearly is a passion for the people who work there. We spent two hours there, finishing with tea in the atmospheric Geoffrey Bawa designed office. I thoroughly enjoyed it and would highly recommend any visitor to the Dambullah area to spend a morning or afternoon there. Not sure how much they charge- I gave a donation and felt it was worth every rupee.

title: Worth a visit
body: There are numerous paths through this arboretum and the plants and trees here are labeled. Unfortunately, we did not allow enough time for this visit and hope that others can give better reports.

title: Intelligent, important, courageous
body: We arrived unannounced and were given a generous welcome. Mr Jayantha Amarasinghe took us on a tour of these amazing woods. He has dedicated himself entirely to continue the work that Sam Popham began and is thus restoring this important forest, one tree at a time. It is not without pain: Mr Amarasinghe showed us a snare poachers had left and we witnessed two suspicious men scaling the wire fence. It takes courage to protect this land but the property is under his watchful eye and he most knowledge about all of Sri Lanka's trees. Note the house on the property: it's by architect Geoffrey Bawa and has a wonderful feel. Later he brought us tea and we share pastries we had brought. One of my best memory of that trip.

title: OSC visit to Sam Popham Arboretum
body: Our small group of 11 students and two teachers enjoyed our night walk at the Arboretum. We were well guided and the path is a very easy walk. My only regret is that we didn't have a chance to return in the daytime to appreciate the trees in daylight.

title: A great lesson for re-forestation
body: The history is already provided by others. What struck me was the demonstration of the ease and simplicity with which indigenous dry-zone tropical forest can be regenerated with minimal interference from man. Popham's techniques could be widely adopted at minimal cost. This place deserves wide recognition and support. If money is not forthcoming from somewhere it is likely to disappear for ever.

title: Wonderful arboretum with lovely story
body: We visited Pophams arboretum for an afternoon before going to the Dambulla caves. It was set up in the 1960s by Sam Popham, ex Navy and ex tea planter. He was concerned over the disappearance of indigenous forest in the dry zone of Sri Lanka so bought a patch of scrub jungle and set about returning it to its natural state. It was clearly a labour of love and he became famous in Sri Lanka, well before environmentalism was mainstream. He lived on the site for over 40 years and saw the native flora thrive with his unique methods. Sadly he had to return to UK due to ill health in the early 2000s and now lives in a care home in Sussex and is in his 90s. The arboretum is a haven for birds and animals including lorises and mouse deer. The current guardian is a lovely and very enthusiastic man who was a disciple of Mr Popham and has worked there for 16 years. Many of the trees are endangered and it is increasingly realised that they have medicinal value and this arboretum needs more support. I entirely agree with the previous reviewers. It is a haven of peace and tranquility . The best time to go for birds is in the early morning and late afternoon.

title: Wonderful place run by wonderful people
body: We visited this place, which is a real treat for nature lovers. We liked it so much that we decided to stay the night there. We went for another walk in the forest in the evening and managed to see a few Lorises and Mouse Deers. We thoroughly enjoyed staying there.

title: Amazing
body: Walk up the steps take your time and soak in the atmosphere, because you'll be glad you did just to see and hear the amazing sights and sounds - Well worth a visit
